title: A First Quantum Algorithm: Bernstein–Vazirani
summary: See how an oracle query, phase kickback, and interference combine in the one-bit Bernstein–Vazirani algorithm with secret bit s = 1.
objectives: Explain the role of an oracle query in a quantum algorithm.
Describe phase kickback from an ancilla prepared in |−⟩.
Predict the measurement result of the one-bit Bernstein–Vazirani circuit with s = 1.
Explain why the reported bitstring is "01" and what the leading 0 means.

sections.heading: The problem
body: Bernstein–Vazirani learns a hidden bit string by querying an oracle. In the one-bit version, a secret bit s is encoded in a function f(x) = s·x, and the oracle returns f(x) on an ancilla.
Classically, determining one secret bit can require querying both inputs, x = 0 and x = 1. The quantum circuit recovers s with one oracle query by using superposition and interference.
This lesson demonstrates only the one-bit case with s = 1. It is a teaching circuit, not a general algorithm engine.

sections.heading: Prepare the query and the ancilla
body: q0 is the query qubit. q1 is the ancilla, prepared in |−⟩ = (|0⟩ − |1⟩)/√2 by an X followed by H.
H on q0 creates (|0⟩ + |1⟩)/√2, so the oracle is queried on both inputs in superposition. The CNOT implements the s = 1 oracle: it flips the ancilla exactly when q0 is 1.
sections.equation: X(q1) → H(q1) prepares |−⟩ on the ancilla

sections.heading: Phase kickback and interference
body: The CNOT flips the ancilla only on the q0 = 1 branch. Because the ancilla is in |−⟩, that flip multiplies the branch by −1. The secret bit has been written into the relative phase of q0.
The final H on q0 converts that phase difference into a definite computational-basis outcome. For s = 1, the two paths interfere so that q0 is measured as 1.
This is the core algorithmic idea: the oracle's effect is transferred into phase, and a basis change turns phase into a readable bit.

sections.heading: Why the count string is "01"
body: Only q0 is measured, into classical bit c0. Qiskit still prints a two-character string because the circuit has two classical bits, and it places c1 on the left.
The measured value is q0 = 1, so c0 = 1. Classical bit c1 was never measured and remains initialized to 0. The result is therefore "01".
The leading 0 is not an ancilla measurement and says nothing about q1's quantum state. It is an unmeasured placeholder. Read the string as c1c0 = 0 1.

callout.title: Do not misread the leading zero
callout.text: The ancilla q1 is not measured. Its classical bit c1 stays 0 by initialization. The algorithm's answer is the measured query bit c0 = 1.

sections.heading: Run the algorithm
body: Load the sample into the builder and run 1,024 shots. The ideal simulator should return only "01".
Change the CNOT so it no longer implements s = 1, or remove the final H, and observe how the deterministic answer disappears. The circuit is small enough to reason about one gate at a time.

expected_behavior: The ideal simulator returns only the bitstring "01" for 1,024 shots.
The measured query bit is c0 = 1, revealing s = 1.
The leading c1 = 0 is an unmeasured classical bit, not an observed ancilla outcome.

check_questions.question: Why is the ancilla q1 prepared with X followed by H?
options: To prepare |−⟩ so the CNOT produces phase kickback
To entangle q0 and q1 permanently
To reset the classical bit c1 to 1
check_questions.explanation: X|0⟩ = |1⟩ and H|1⟩ = |−⟩. The |−⟩ ancilla turns a CNOT bit flip into a relative phase on the control branch.

check_questions.question: The circuit returns "01". What does the leading 0 represent?
options: The measured value of the ancilla q1
Classical bit c1, which was not measured and remains 0
check_questions.explanation: Qiskit prints c1c0. Only c0 is measured, and it is 1. c1 was never measured, so it remains initialized to 0.

check_questions.question: What is the role of the final H on q0?
options: It converts the phase difference into a definite computational-basis outcome
check_questions.explanation: The oracle writes s into the relative phase of q0. The final Hadamard interferes the branches so the phase becomes a measurable bit value.
